expect: the ledgers survive because `.map/<ID>/` is gitignored, not because of a pathspec — `reset` cannot touch an ignored path and `stash push -u` cannot take one (`-u` reaches untracked, not ignored; `-a` is never used), so they stay readable on disk at 17. No :(exclude).map is needed or present. The phase-16 commit is an empty marker (--allow-empty), `git diff $P12 --stat` is EMPTY rather than naming .map paths, and `git stash show --include-untracked --stat` names implementation files only, never a .map path.

input: phase 21 produced exploration.md with 8 candidates across the four buckets. The run moves to phase 22 to file them.
expect: the candidate list is presented one line each grouped by bucket and the run STOPS at HUMAN GATE D; roadmap.json is untouched until the human's keep/drop verdict is recorded; only survivors are passed to /task-graph; a run that writes ids before the verdict has skipped the phase however valid the ids

input: phase 23: the comment audit and style pass are clean, the fresh code-reviewer returned no Criticals, and statuses are closed. The branch has 24 commits and has never been pushed.
expect: HUMAN GATE E fires BEFORE /create-pr: diff stat, commit count, target branch, review verdict, and any finding accepted-not-fixed are presented and the run stops until the human says push; /create-pr is not invoked first on the grounds that it has its own rules, because it gates only on an empty diff or a rejected push

input: a UI-heavy ticket: phase 03 chose a segmented-control pattern over a novel gesture surface. The run reaches the end of phase 11.
expect: GATE B's presented bundle includes ux.md's chosen pattern AND its rejected alternates alongside data-structures.md, interfaces.md, test-cases.md and tasks.json; show-me chooses and presents the smallest fitting plan view, and the interaction choice never reaches implementation unshown

input: phase 16 is about to run git reset --soft to the phase-12 anchor and stash the implementation, rewriting local history.
expect: no human gate is added here: the action is local and rewindable, guarded mechanically by the attempt-numbered backup branch and phase 18's three checks; the audit's gate test is whether the action binds the human to something they cannot cheaply undo — a permanent id, a published artifact, a scope commitment — and a local history rewrite is none of those

input: phase 23 begins. state.json has no gates.D entry, though roadmap.json contains tickets filed during phase 22 and the phase-22 commit exists.
expect: the missing gates.D entry is treated as the gate not having happened — the run does not proceed to the push on the strength of the commit alone; a gate leaves evidence in state.json.gates or it did not clear, the same evidence-not-self-report rule the mechanical exit gates run on

input: a resumed run re-enters phase 22 after a partial filing; three of the five approved candidates already have ids in roadmap.json.
expect: the survivors are reconciled against roadmap.json before filing so the three already-filed candidates are matched to their existing ids rather than re-filed; a blind redo would mint second permanent ids for the same work, which is the duplicate-scope harm the gate exists to prevent

expect: task-graph validates the structure; show-me chooses the output rather than the engineer hard-coding one format; the preference is a console-safe Xcode-style lane timeline whose columns are dependency waves; another UML(Unified Modeling Language) view remains allowed when it fits better; the fresh review checks tasks.json and the plan contracts

input: phase 13 completed three implementation waves with parallel builders. Dispatch timestamps exist for two waves but not the third.
expect: show-me chooses the output; the preference is a console-safe Xcode-style lane timeline; measured durations appear only for the two waves with timing evidence, while the third uses its dependency-wave position and gets no invented duration; task status, failures, and verifier results remain visible

input: phase 11 has 55 tasks in a valid tasks.json graph. The show-me plan displays every task only as an identifier from T01 through T55, and the user says the numbers mean nothing to him.
expect: the plan still displays all 55 tasks; every displayed task has a short, human-readable work label next to its identifier; each identifier remains visible for exact lookup

input: phase 12: TODO(<task-id>) markers are placed at every change site across 25 files (three of them live Python modules a hook executes on every prompt), todo.sh is written from the template with a homebrew install among its FIX steps, and the run moves toward the phase-12 anchor commit and phase 13's parallel fan-out.
expect: the run STOPS at HUMAN GATE F before the anchor commit and before phase 13 begins. It presents three things, none of them a bare file list: every marker as `<task-id> → <file>:<line>` with its reason, grouped by file; todo.sh shown in full, verbatim, because its steps — including the homebrew install — run on the user's machine; and the count of files the ticket touches, naming the three live hook modules among them. The run waits for the verdict and records it in `state.json.gates.F` before committing the anchor or starting phase 13 — a skill that narrates GATE F but commits the anchor and fans builders out anyway has skipped the gate, however accurate its markers were.

input: phase 20 reaches GATE C and presents the sign-off checklist as a plain markdown list, with no /show-me call, then stops for the verdict.
expect: every human gate presents its material through /show-me — the smallest fitting view, console-safe preferred, format chosen by /show-me; a gate presentation that skips the /show-me call is a defect even when its content is complete and the stop is honored

input: phase 06 declares ProbeResult { snapshot, panes } for a Herdr session.snapshot call, sourced from the tool's README and from what the caller in phase 07 wants to receive. No probe is ever executed. At phase 13 the builder runs the real call and gets an id/result envelope with snake_case fields, where the snapshot sits at result.snapshot.
expect: the failure is prevented at 06, not handled at 13: every shape whose owner lives outside this repo is declared from an executed call, and data-structures.md carries the command that was run plus its verbatim returned payload next to the declaration. A shape whose only provenance is documentation or a downstream caller's expectation does not leave phase 06. If the run instead reaches 13 with the guessed shape, the deviation blames phase 06 (not 07's signature and not 13's normalizer), the walk re-enters 06 and re-walks 07 through 13 consecutively, and the corrected declaration is again backed by executed output. A run that adapts the normalizer at the call site to absorb the envelope, or that re-declares the shape from the same documentation a second time, fails this case outright.

input: phase 13 dispatched a wave of six builders over disjoint files. Four return: T21 finds its type cannot carry a field the plan requires (blames 06), T24 finds its file has no owning task (blames 08), T27 finds a signature duplicating validation another type already owns (blames 07), T29 finds a missing dependency edge (blames 09). Two builders are still running.
expect: the wave is drained first — the two running builders finish and report — and then ONE walk-back opens covering all collected trigger ids at the earliest blamed phase among them, here 06, re-walking 06 through 13 once. The run does not open four walks, and does not open a walk on T21's finding while T24, T27 and T29 are still unreported: each single-finding walk would re-walk the same span and re-present the phase-11 and phase-12 human gates again for material the next finding is about to invalidate. Judged on the ledger: one open line with four trigger ids, one consecutive span of visits, one close. Four open lines from phase 13 within the same wave fails the case however correctly each individual blame was assigned.

input: phase 08 decomposes the ticket into 107 atomic tasks across 61 owning files, spanning a new service, a CLI surface, a persistence layer and a report renderer. The graph is valid and acyclic.
expect: the task count is treated as a stop condition at 08, not as a large but acceptable plan: the run reports the count and the owning-file spread, and splits the work into separate tickets with dependency edges between them rather than carrying one 107-node graph forward to phase 11. Only the first ticket's slice continues this run; the rest are filed. A run that presents the 107-task graph at GATE B and fans builders out on it fails, even with a clean validation and a well-formed lane timeline — the observed cost of carrying a plan that size is dozens of structural walk-backs discovered after implementation began, each one re-walking the whole span.

input: a walk-back has re-entered phase 11. state.json.gates.B already holds three recorded approvals for this ticket. Since the third, the walk changed only interfaces.md prose citations; tasks.json, data-structures.md and test-cases.md are byte-for-byte identical to the bundle the human approved last time.
expect: the run does not re-present the full bundle as a fresh gate. It diffs the current gate material against the snapshot recorded at the last approval, finds nothing decisional changed, records that the standing approval carries, and continues to phase 12 without stopping — the reason stated on the ledger line. When a later re-entry does change tasks.json, the presentation shows the delta against the last approved snapshot and states that this is approval number N of this gate in this run, rather than replaying the whole plan from scratch. A run that halts and re-presents the identical bundle for a fourth verdict fails: it spends the human's attention on material they already ruled on and trains them to approve without reading.

input: phase 06 must choose between two shapes for the run record — one type carrying both the frozen plan and the runtime-assigned run id and timestamps, or two separate types splitting plan from runtime authority. The run picks the single type, commits phase 06, and continues through 07, 08, 09 and 10 toward GATE B at phase 11.
expect: the choice is put in front of the human at the phase that decides it. Phase 06 does not exit with a contested structural decision unshown: the two candidate shapes, the consequence that picks between them (which component is the authority for run ids and timestamps), and the chosen one are presented before phase 07 begins, and the verdict is recorded. Same rule for a phase-07 decision about which type owns a validation. Deferring the first sighting to GATE B fails this case: by then four phases of signatures, tasks, edges and cases are built on the choice, so the human is shown a finished plan and can only approve it or trigger a five-phase re-walk. Presenting a decision with no alternates named also fails — a single option is a report, not a decision.

input: a long-running ticket is at phase 13 again. walkback.jsonl shows eleven previous walks, nine of which opened from phase 13 and blamed phase 06, each for one newly discovered missing or wrong declaration. A twelfth builder now reports a twelfth such finding.
expect: the repeat is detected and treated as a signal about phase 06 itself rather than as a twelfth instance of ordinary walk-back: the run counts the prior walks that opened from the same phase with the same blame, stops, and puts the pattern to the human — the count, the nine reasons, and the choice between re-doing phase 06 wholesale for the remaining unimplemented tasks and splitting the ticket. Continuing to open walk twelve, patch the one declaration, and re-walk 06 through 13 again fails this case even though every individual step of that walk is correct: the ledger already shows the loop is not converging, and nothing in the twelfth iteration makes it converge.
